title: Replete topos of sheaves on a site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal T=\Sh(\mathcal C)$. An *inverse sequence* in
$\mathcal T$ is a functor $\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal T$, i.e. sheaves $F_n$
($n\ge0$) with transition maps $t_n\colon F_{n+1}\to F_n$. Its limit is the sheaf

$$
\Bigl(\varprojlim_nF_n\Bigr)(V)=\Bigl\{(x_n)\in\prod_nF_n(V):t_n(x_{n+1})=x_n\ \text{for all }n\Bigr\},
$$

with projections $p_m\colon\varprojlim_nF_n\to F_m$, $(x_n)\mapsto x_m$. A morphism of
sheaves $\varphi\colon F\to G$ is an *epimorphism* if it is locally surjective: for every
$V$ and $y\in G(V)$ there is a covering $\{V_k\to V\}$ and $x_k\in F(V_k)$ with
$\varphi(x_k)=y|_{V_k}$. The topos $\mathcal T$ is *replete* if, whenever all $t_n$ are
epimorphisms, every $p_m$ is an epimorphism.

proof.text: Use the site, sheaf and natural-transformation conventions of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (1). For the maps $t_n:F_{n+1}\to F_n$, the map from $F_b$ to $F_a$ for $a<b$ is the finite composite $t_a\circ\cdots\circ t_{b-1}$; for $a=b$ it is the identity. Associativity gives the functor $\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal T$. Let $L(V)$ be the displayed set of compatible tuples and restrict each coordinate along a map $V'\to V$. Naturality of $t_n$ implies that the restricted tuple is compatible, so this defines a presheaf with natural coordinate projections. For any set $S$ with compatible maps $q_n:S\to F_n(V)$, the unique map $S\to L(V)$ inducing them is $s\mapsto(q_n(s))_n$. Thus the displayed set, with its projections, is the limit of the section diagram; compatibility with adjacent transitions implies compatibility with every finite composite.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] (1) to the small index category $\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the diagram in step 1. It says that the sectionwise limit presheaf $L$ is a sheaf and that its coordinate projections form a limit in $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ and in presheaves. Explicitly, a compatible cone of sheaf morphisms $q_n:H\to F_n$ induces $q_V:H(V)\to L(V)$ by $s\mapsto(q_{n,V}(s))_n$; this is natural since every $q_n$ is natural, and it is unique since its coordinates are prescribed. In particular the projections $p_m$ in the definition are actual sheaf morphisms. This uses no surjectivity hypothesis on the transitions.

source.place: Tag 00W2, lemma-limit-sheaf and proof; sectionwise compatible tuples specialized to the countable inverse sequence

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] to an arbitrary morphism $\varphi:F\to G$ in this same category of set-valued sheaves. Its statement identifies right-cancellability with the covering-and-local-lifts condition displayed in the definition. Consequently the word epimorphism used both for $t_n$ and for $p_m$ agrees with the categorical notion. With the limit and projections from step 2, repleteness is the predicate that for every such inverse sequence, local surjectivity of every transition implies local surjectivity of every projection $p_m$. This is exactly the repleteness clause in the unit; it does not assert that every site has this property.
